extracted.intended_audience: researchers and grant applicants preparing proposals for NIH, NSF, foundations and similar funders (including early-career investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, archive-derived guidance and implicit evaluation criteria for writing competitive research grant applications across funders (NIH, NSF, GRFP, foundations). Emphasizes Specific Aims, methodology, investigator framing, visuals, and funder-specific priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open with the question or knowledge gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin Specific Aims / Project Summary by stating the question or knowledge gap the project addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the opening so reviewers immediately understand the problem; this is a repeatedly observed feature of successful applications in the archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-2 sentence elevator pitch before details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise 1–2 sentence summary (an 'elevator pitch') early, prior to detailed aims or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this pitch to orient non-specialist reviewers and panelists; make it clear and compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name the central hypothesis explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: State the central hypothesis of the project explicitly in the Specific Aims or Project Summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis-driven framing helps distinguish mechanistic proposals from descriptive work and is frequently present in funded apps.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2–4 numbered aims with clear logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 2–4 numbered aims that are logically connected and independently informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep aims independent enough to avoid cascade failure (no co-dependent aims); reviewers expect clear logic and sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing impact statement
rubrics_metrics.description: End Specific Aims / Project Summary with a clear statement of the potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie results to significance and broader consequences relevant to the funder or field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage-appropriate scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Match the project's scope to the investigator's career stage (e.g., ESI vs. mid/senior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-career applicants should avoid overreach; funded apps demonstrate realistic, stage-appropriate ambitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity proportionate to grant size
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate a publication/productivity record proportionate to the requested award size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists gauge whether the investigator's track record justifies the requested budget and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence narrative for early-career investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly present evidence of independence (distinct research direction, leadership, funding potential) for early-career applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe independence in the biosketch/personal statement and name collaborators/mentors with defined roles without suggesting dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track-record narrative for mid/senior investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: For established investigators, craft a narrative that highlights leadership, prior success, and the trajectory that justifies the new work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link past accomplishments to capability to execute the proposed research and to mentor/lead larger projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific named collaborators with roles
rubrics_metrics.description: List collaborators by name and specify their roles and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague statements about 'collaboration' — name who will do what and why they are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite published protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference published methods/protocols rather than only describing novel or in-house procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing established protocols increases reviewers' confidence in feasibility and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify your approach over alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the chosen methods are preferable to reasonable alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate reviewer questions by comparing approaches and justifying choices with evidence or rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power calculations with effect-size citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include power/sample-size calculations and cite effect sizes or prior data used to justify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing or unjustified power calculations are flagged as weaknesses; tie calculations to preliminary data or literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan with multiple-comparison correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statistical analysis plan, including procedures for correcting multiple comparisons where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail primary endpoints, statistical tests, and correction approaches; general statements about 'statistics will be applied' are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify biological and technical replicates
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the number and type (biological vs technical) of replicates to be used in experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear replication plans allow reviewers to judge robustness and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication/validation of key reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plans for authentication or validation of critical reagents (e.g., cell lines, antibodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses rigor and reproducibility expectations (especially post-2016 NIH guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual figure in Significance / Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a conceptual figure in the Significance or Background to illustrate hypotheses, mechanisms, or models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-designed concept figure helps non-specialist reviewers grasp the project quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative preliminary data figures demonstrating feasibility and supporting aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded applications often include solid quantitative pilot results rather than only qualitative descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline (Gantt-style) figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a timeline/Gantt-style figure showing milestones and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines demonstrate feasibility and realistic sequencing of tasks; reviewers check timelines against aims and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schematic of overall research strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall schematic showing how aims, methods, and analyses interrelate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A schematic clarifies the research strategy and helps reviewers assess coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of Personal Statement / Biosketch content across applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors commonly reuse personal statement and biosketch sections when applying to related opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuse is acceptable if updated to reflect the target funder's priorities; maintain accuracy and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse of methodology blocks across related projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology descriptions may be repurposed across similar proposals, with updates as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methods are tailored to the specific aims and reviewer expectations of each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator narratives persist with updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Core investigator narratives (independence, track record) often persist across resubmissions, but should be updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep narratives current (new publications, awards) and tuned to the funding program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance framing adapts to funder priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applicants adapt their significance and impact arguments to match what the funder values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research the funder's stated priorities and language; tailor examples and impact statements accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start 6+ months earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin proposal preparation at least six months before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archive authors stress lead time for iterations, gathering preliminary data, and securing letters and institutional approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get program officer feedback at idea stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult program officers early to vet fit and get guidance on scope and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO feedback can clarify funder expectations and improve alignment; many successful applicants consulted POs early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a mock-review committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a mock-review committee to get candid, external critique before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mock reviews help identify clarity problems and methodological weaknesses reviewers will spot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read funded applications in your area before drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Study funded examples in your field to learn structure, tone, and level of evidence expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Grants recommends reading funded apps as models for good practices and funder-specific preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate Specific Aims extensively (10+ times)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine Specific Aims repeatedly (archive authors suggest iterating 10+ times) before finalizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims undergo the most revision and are critical for initial reviewer impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being too ambitious for early-stage investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not propose a scope that exceeds what is realistic for an early-stage investigator (ESI) or first R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overambitious scope is a common reason for rejection; align aims with experience and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid co-dependent aims (independence of aims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design aims so that failure of one does not invalidate the entire project (no cascade dependence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent aims increase chances that reviewers see value even if one aim is partially unsuccessful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient methodological detail for reviewers to evaluate feasibility and rigor; avoid vague plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vagueness in methods is repeatedly cited by unsuccessful applicants as a key weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address rigor explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Directly discuss rigor and reproducibility measures (blinding, randomization, sample handling) where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor language has been mandatory/expected, especially in NIH submissions after 2016; failure to address it is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to non-specialist reviewers (avoid hyper-specialist jargon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make writing accessible to reviewers outside the immediate subfield; reviewers can be generalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is especially important for NSF GRFP and panel-based reviews where a generalist perspective is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims are the most-iterated document (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: On NIH applications, the Specific Aims page is revised most and is crucial for reviewer impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest substantial effort into the Aims page; it often determines whether reviewers continue reading with interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach section is where most points are lost (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH reviewers often deduct points in the Approach section; it is a critical scrutiny area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit experimental design, alternatives, limitations, and mitigation strategies in Approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission is common (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission after initial rejection is the norm rather than exception at NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summary statements and reviewer feedback to iteratively improve and resubmit; archive shows many successful resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility language mandatory (post-2016 NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-2016 NIH expectations require explicit discussion of rigor and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address authentication, sample-size justification, blinding/randomization where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary read by every panelist (NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF panelists commonly read the Project Summary; it should be clear and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft the Project Summary to communicate Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts concisely to all panelists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts carry equal weight (NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF evaluates proposals on two criteria of equal weight: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, specific Broader Impacts activities and clear evidence of intellectual merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts must be specific with named activities (NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF Broader Impacts statements should list specific activities and responsible parties where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic claims; include named programs, outreach activities, or measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description is short — every paragraph must justify itself (NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF Project Descriptions are concise; each paragraph should have a clear purpose and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim filler and ensure each paragraph advances intellectual merit or broader impacts arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement carries majority weight (NSF GRFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: For NSF GRFP, the personal statement accounts for a large portion of review weight (archive notes ~60%+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft the personal statement to demonstrate potential, leadership, and fit; reviewers are highly influenced by it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan demonstrates ability not commitment (NSF GRFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: GRFP Research Plans are evaluated for the applicant's ability to carry out research, not as binding commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show competence, feasibility, and training potential rather than promising a fully specified multi-year program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write accessibly for generalist reviewers (NSF GRFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: GRFP reviewers are often generalists; write clearly and avoid assuming specialist knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain significance and approach in plain language and provide conceptual figures or analogies as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation matter (NSF GRFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong, specific letters are influential for NSF GRFP decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek recommender letters that address intellectual merit, broader impacts, and the applicant's potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read foundation annual reports and match portfolios (foundations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying to foundations, study their annual report and funded portfolio to ensure alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundations expect close fit with program priorities; proposal alignment increases competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officers at foundations are often accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Many foundations have accessible program officers; contact them to discuss fit and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conversations to tailor applications to program goals and to learn any unstated preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller foundations: less competitive but smaller awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller foundations may have lower applicant competition but correspondingly smaller award sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance competitiveness and budget expectations when targeting smaller funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear question with significance (implicit funded-app criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded applications demonstrate a clearly stated research question with substantial significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine a clear gap statement, significance framing, and a persuasive impact narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven approach (implicit funded-app criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applications are often hypothesis-driven rather than purely descriptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure aims and experiments to test specific hypotheses with measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent aims (no failure cascade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims should be designed so one aim's failure does not invalidate the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft aims to each contribute meaningful knowledge independently to protect overall project value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data present
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded proposals commonly include quantitative preliminary data that support feasibility and effect sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative data strengthen power/sample-size justifications and confidence in methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology specific enough to evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods should be described in sufficient detail for reviewers to evaluate feasibility and rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid high-level statements; include concrete steps, controls, and potential pitfalls with mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific statistical analysis plan is expected, not generic promises of analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define endpoints, models, covariates, handling of missing data, and multiple-testing corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator–environment match
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the investigator and institutional environment together provide needed expertise and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show institutional support, core facilities, and administrative backing appropriate for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets and timelines should be realistic and consistent with the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Padded budgets or unrealistic schedules are common reasons for rejection; tie costs to specific aims and milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder-priority alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that clearly align with funder priorities or recent funded portfolios fare better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the project maps onto the funder's goals and cite relevant programmatic calls or priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vague significance ('important') is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing aims as simply 'important' without specific context is flagged as vague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make significance concrete: describe the gap, affected populations/fields, and measurable benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive rather than hypothesis-driven aims is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that are primarily descriptive without testable hypotheses are less competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, recast descriptive aims into hypothesis-testing or mechanistic frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient or qualitative preliminary data is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying solely on qualitative or minimal preliminary data reduces confidence in feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, add quantitative pilot data or justify why such data are not feasible before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing power calculation is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting power/sample-size justification is a common and serious flaw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include calculations or strong rationale for sample sizes, referencing effect-size literature when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator overreach for career stage is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposing a scope beyond what is reasonable for the PI's career stage undermines reviewer confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale aims and leadership expectations to demonstrated experience and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Padded budget is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Unjustified or inflated budgets are noticed and penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify each cost item; reviewers compare requested resources against proposed activities and timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrealistic timeline is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines that compress complex activities or not align with aims are criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed timeline with milestones and contingencies that matches the scope and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mismatch with funder priorities is a weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting work that does not fit the funder's stated priorities leads to poor competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research calls, program descriptions, and past awards to ensure fit before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymized funded applications preferred for sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Grants prefers that shared funded applications be anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymization protects privacy while allowing others to learn structure and substance from successful examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author commentary on what worked / didn't
rubrics_metrics.description: Archive entries should include author commentary explaining why elements succeeded or failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual commentary helps readers interpret archived applications beyond the raw text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share reviewers' summary statements where shareable
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reviewers' summary statements when permitted to provide insight into decision rationales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements illuminate reviewer concerns and help applicants prioritize revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include timeline of submission to funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the timeline from initial submission through resubmissions to funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles of submission history help prospective applicants understand realistic timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include resubmission history when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing resubmission history provides transparency about iterative improvements and reviewer responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmission histories show how applications evolved and what changes led to success.
